Bangladesh surveys of the DHS Program

Source: R/data.R
bdhs_surveys.Rd

Catalogue of the 13 Bangladesh surveys distributed by the DHS Program: the nine Demographic and Health Surveys (1993-94 to 2022), the three Service Provision Assessments (1999-2000, 2014, 2017) and the 2001 Maternal Health Services and Maternal Mortality Survey (BMMS, survey type "OTH").

Usage

bdhs_surveys

Format

A tibble with 13 rows (one per survey) and 29 columns:

survey_id

DHS survey identifier, e.g. "BD2017DHS"; the key used throughout the package (see bdhs_survey_id()).

survey_type

"DHS", "SPA" or "OTH" (BMMS 2001).

survey_year

Survey year as used in the survey id (end year of the fieldwork for surveys spanning two years).

survey_label

Year label used by the DHS Program, e.g. "2017-18".

survey_num

Numeric DHS survey number (SurveyNum); also the survey key of the DHS Spatial Data Repository.

recode_version

Two-character version code of the survey's recode files, e.g. "7R" in BDIR7RFL.

dhs_phase

DHS phase (first digit of recode_version).

has_indicator_data

Whether the DHS API publishes indicator values for the survey (only the nine DHS rounds; see bdhs_indicators).

status

Survey status in the DHS API.

fieldwork_start, fieldwork_end

First and last month of fieldwork (dates set to the first day of the month).

publication_date, release_date

Dates of the final report and of the data release.

implementing_org

Implementing organization(s).

n_clusters

Number of sample points (clusters, PSUs); for SPAs, the number of facilities in the sample.

n_households

Number of households interviewed.

women_universe

Population of the women's questionnaire (always "Ever Married Women" for the DHS rounds).

n_women

Number of women interviewed.

women_age_min, women_age_max

Age range of eligible women (10-49 in 1993-94 to 2004 and 12-49 in 2011; DHS indicators refer to women 15-49).

men_universe

Population of the men's questionnaire, if any.

n_men

Number of men interviewed.

men_age_min, men_age_max

Age range of eligible men.

n_facilities

Number of facilities: SPA facilities, or for the 1993-94 and 1996-97 DHS the facilities of the service availability survey.

footnotes

DHS API footnotes about the survey.

characteristic_ids

List column of DHS survey-characteristic ids (topics covered, e.g. anthropometry, biomarkers).

report_url

URL of the survey's final report (PDF).

indicators_updated

Date of the most recent revision of the survey's indicator values in the DHS API, if any was announced.

Source

The DHS Program Indicator Data API, https://api.dhsprogram.com (surveys, datasets, publications, surveycharacteristics and dataupdates endpoints), API version 8.1, retrieved 2026-10-26. Built by data-raw/01-fetch-dhs-api.R and data-raw/02-build-api-datasets.R.

Details

Every BDHS women's sample is a sample of ever-married women; see women_universe. bdhs_rounds() gives a compact version of this table that does not depend on the bundled data.

See also

bdhs_rounds(), bdhs_survey_id(), bdhs_datasets, bdhs_indicators.

Examples

bdhs_surveys[, c("survey_id", "survey_label", "n_clusters", "n_women")]
#> # A tibble: 13 × 4
#>    survey_id survey_label n_clusters n_women
#>    <chr>     <chr>             <int>   <int>
#>  1 BD1994DHS 1993-94             301    9640
#>  2 BD1997DHS 1996-97             313    9127
#>  3 BD1999SPA 1999-00             341      NA
#>  4 BD2000DHS 1999-00             341   10544
#>  5 BD2001OTH 2001                808  103796
#>  6 BD2004DHS 2004                361   11440
#>  7 BD2007DHS 2007                361   10996
#>  8 BD2011DHS 2011                600   17842
#>  9 BD2014DHS 2014                600   17863
#> 10 BD2014SPA 2014               1548      NA
#> 11 BD2017DHS 2017-18             672   20127
#> 12 BD2017SPA 2017               1600      NA
#> 13 BD2022DHS 2022                675   30078

# Rounds with official indicator values
bdhs_surveys$survey_id[bdhs_surveys$has_indicator_data]
#> [1] "BD1994DHS" "BD1997DHS" "BD2000DHS" "BD2004DHS" "BD2007DHS" "BD2011DHS"
#> [7] "BD2014DHS" "BD2017DHS" "BD2022DHS"
